krokkleiva_kongeveien.desc: Historic road line up Krokkleiva between Sundvollen and Krokskogen, part of the Bergen Royal Road. The place shows travel, post, trade, tourism and control of the passage between the Oslo area and Ringerike.
krokkleiva_kongeveien.popupDesc: Krokkleiva is one of the clearest historic road sections in Buskerud. The road climbs from Sundvollen toward Krokskogen and formed part of the connection between the capital area, Ringerike and further west. In History Go, Krokkleiva should be used to read road as cultural heritage: terrain, stonework, gradient, travel routes and who actually had to walk or drive here.

bragernes_kirke.name: Bragernes Church
bragernes_kirke.desc: Neo-Gothic church built after the town fire at Bragernes in 1866 and consecrated in 1871. Bragernes Church shows Drammen’s reconstruction, urban plan, civic confidence and 19th-century church architecture.
bragernes_kirke.popupDesc: Bragernes Church is a key place for understanding modern Drammen after the town fire in 1866. The church was consecrated in 1871 and stands as a clear symbol in the cityscape. In History Go, the place should be used to show how disasters could create new urban plans, new architecture and new public spaces.

riddergarden_honefoss.name: Riddergården Hønefoss
riddergarden_honefoss.desc: Historic town farm in Hønefoss with roots in trade, farming and local urban life before and during the emergence of Hønefoss as an industrial place. Riddergården makes Ringerike’s trade and everyday life concrete.
riddergarden_honefoss.popupDesc: Riddergården in Hønefoss is an important local cultural environment because it shows urban and trading life in an area often told through Ringerike’s saga, church and industrial traces. In History Go, Riddergården should be used as a concrete entry into Hønefoss as a historical place, not only as a modern town centre.

modum_bad_st_olafs_kilde.name: Modum Bad / St. Olaf’s Spring
modum_bad_st_olafs_kilde.desc: Health and institutional site in Modum, where the spa St. Olafs Bad opened in 1857. Modum Bad shows the transition from healing spring and spa to modern treatment institution.
modum_bad_st_olafs_kilde.popupDesc: Modum Bad has a long and layered history: the story of St. Olaf’s spring, the spa that opened in 1857, prominent guests, institutional changes and later development into a modern treatment site. In History Go, the place should be used as health history and institutional history: how nature, water, faith, medicine, rest, class, treatment and professionalization have been understood differently over time.

nore_i_kraftverk.name: Nore I Power Station
nore_i_kraftverk.desc: Large state hydropower station in Numedal, commissioned in 1928 to supply power to Eastern Norway. Nore I shows hydropower, dam history, interwar engineering and state-led modernization.
nore_i_kraftverk.popupDesc: Nore I Power Station is a key site in Norwegian hydropower history. The plant was commissioned in 1928 and uses the drop between Tunhovdfjorden and Rødberg. The development required dams, penstocks, a power station, construction work, roads, railway, housing and a new local community around Rødberg. In History Go, Nore I should be used to explain how mountain water, the state, technology, labour and Eastern Norway’s need for power were linked in one modernization project.

sundvollen_hotell_skysskifte.name: Sundvollen Hotel / coaching station
sundvollen_hotell_skysskifte.desc: Historic lodging and coaching-station site at the foot of Krokkleiva. Sundvollen shows travel, post, trade, innkeeping, tourism and the connection between Ringerike and the capital region.
sundvollen_hotell_skysskifte.popupDesc: Sundvollen has a long history as a stopping place on the important travel route across Krokskogen. Before railways, cars and modern roads, such coaching stations and inns were necessary parts of the infrastructure: people, horses, goods, post and news had to rest, change and be organized. In History Go, Sundvollen should be used together with Krokkleiva to explain how travel actually worked in earlier times, and how a hotel can be transport history, not just accommodation.

union_papirfabrikk_drammen.name: Union Paper Mill / Grønland Drammen
union_papirfabrikk_drammen.desc: Former paper and industrial environment at Grønland in Drammen, later transformed into a culture and knowledge district. Union shows the river city, industrial labour, paper production and new uses for old factory landscapes.
union_papirfabrikk_drammen.popupDesc: The Union area at Grønland in Drammen is an important urban-industrial heritage environment. The paper and wood-processing industry was part of Drammen’s long history as a river, timber and industrial city. When the area was later transformed for culture, education and urban development, the industrial landscape was given a new function. In History Go, the site should be used to show how old factories can be read both as workplaces, production sites and modern urban spaces.

solberg_spinderi.name: Solberg Spinning Mill
solberg_spinderi.desc: Historic textile-industry site by the Solberg River, with spinning mill, workers’ environment, hydropower and industrial community. Solberg Spinderi shows another part of Buskerud’s industrial history than mining, timber and paper.
solberg_spinderi.popupDesc: Solberg Spinderi is an important textile and labour-history site in Buskerud. The spinning mill used hydropower and local labour, and the industrial site around the factory shaped housing, everyday life, working hours, gendered work roles and local community. In History Go, Solberg Spinderi should be used to show the place of the textile industry in modernization: not only raw materials and machines, but families, workers and an entire factory settlement.

lier_sykehus_historisk_omrade.name: Lier Hospital / historic area
lier_sykehus_historisk_omrade.desc: Historic hospital area in Lier, linked to the institutional history of psychiatry in the 20th century. The site must be treated carefully, with emphasis on architecture, social attitudes, treatment and institutional critique.
lier_sykehus_historisk_omrade.popupDesc: Lier Hospital is a difficult but relevant history point. Large psychiatric institutions shaped Norwegian health and social history through the 20th century, both as treatment sites, workplaces, local communities and places where power was exercised. In History Go, Lier Hospital should be used carefully: not as a ghost site or sensation, but as an entry point to institutional history, views of humanity, architecture, treatment, patient rights, the dismantling of large institutions and critical reflection.

vikersund_stasjon_randsfjordbanen.name: Vikersund Station / Randsfjord Line
vikersund_stasjon_randsfjordbanen.desc: Railway junction on the Randsfjord Line, opened in 1866 and later the starting point for the Krøderen Line. Vikersund station shows how the railway connected Modum, Drammen, Krøderen and the inland region.
vikersund_stasjon_randsfjordbanen.popupDesc: Vikersund station is a transport-history junction in Buskerud. The Randsfjord Line opened through the area in 1866, and the Krøderen Line later started here. The station connected industry, agriculture, lake traffic, tourism, post and passenger transport. In History Go, Vikersund should be used to explain how the railway changed distances, markets and travel routes between Drammen, Modum, Krøderen and Hallingdal.

domkirkeodden_hamar.name: Domkirkeodden / Hamar Cathedral ruins
domkirkeodden_hamar.desc: Medieval area at Domkirkeodden in Hamar, with the ruins of Hamar Cathedral and traces of bishopric, town, church power and the Reformation era. The site is one of Innlandet’s clear main points for medieval history.
domkirkeodden_hamar.popupDesc: Domkirkeodden is one of the strongest historic sites in Innlandet. Medieval Hamar lay here, with cathedral, bishop’s residence, church power, urban life and connections to Lake Mjøsa. The cathedral ruins, protective structure and museum make the site physically readable as a medieval town, power centre and memorial landscape. In History Go, Domkirkeodden should be used to explain diocese, Reformation, ruins, urban foundations and how an inland place could be a central ecclesiastical and political hub.

maihaugen_lillehammer.name: Maihaugen
maihaugen_lillehammer.desc: Large open-air museum in Lillehammer, built from Anders Sandvig’s collections. Maihaugen shows Norwegian building traditions, farm and urban life, crafts, homes, modernization and everyday culture from many time layers.
maihaugen_lillehammer.popupDesc: Maihaugen is one of Norway’s most important cultural-history museums. Anders Sandvig’s collections became the basis for an open-air museum where houses, farmyards, interiors, workshops, urban environments and newer homes show how people lived, worked and organized everyday life. In History Go, Maihaugen should be used as a national interpretation point for material culture: buildings as sources, objects as everyday archives, and the transition from farming society to modern Norway.

ringebu_stavkirke.name: Ringebu Stave Church
ringebu_stavkirke.desc: Stave church in Gudbrandsdalen, built in the 13th century and later rebuilt. Ringebu Stave Church shows medieval church building, pilgrimage route, local alterations and its role as an election church in 1814.
ringebu_stavkirke.popupDesc: Ringebu Stave Church is one of Innlandet’s most central medieval buildings. The present stave church was erected in the 13th century and later received a cruciform plan and tower through rebuilding. The church stands at a Gudbrandsdalen church site along historic travel and pilgrimage routes, and it also served as an election church in 1814. In History Go, the site should be used for stave construction, time layers, pilgrimage, local use and how medieval churches could gain new political roles in modern times.

lom_stavkirke.name: Lom Stave Church
lom_stavkirke.desc: Large stave church in Lom, with a medieval core from the 12th century and later alterations. The church is a historic centre point in Ottadalen and shows mountain community, church power, craftsmanship and pilgrimage/travel culture.
lom_stavkirke.popupDesc: Lom Stave Church is a key point in the medieval history of Gudbrandsdalen. The medieval stave construction, later extensions, interior, portals and location in Lom show how a church could be a sacred space, local centre, craft work and marker of identity. In History Go, the site should be used for stave technique, mountain community, travel between valleys and mountains, and the relationship between medieval heritage and a living local community.

kongsvinger_festning.name: Kongsvinger Fortress
kongsvinger_festning.desc: Border fortress by the Glomma and Vinger road, built from 1682 to secure traffic and defence against Sweden. Kongsvinger Fortress shows border politics, military strategy, Øvrebyen and inland defence.
kongsvinger_festning.popupDesc: Kongsvinger Fortress lies strategically above the Glomma and the old travel lines between Norway and Sweden. The fortress was built from 1682 at a place where border, river, road and military control met. Around the fortress, Øvrebyen grew into a distinctive urban environment. In History Go, Kongsvinger Fortress should be used to show that Innlandet is also borderland: defence to the east, trade, military administration, urban development and the relationship between Norway and Sweden.

aulestad_bjornson.name: Aulestad / Bjørnstjerne Bjørnson’s home
aulestad_bjornson.desc: Bjørnstjerne Bjørnson’s home in Gausdal from 1875. Aulestad shows how literature, politics, nation-building, farming, public life and private home could be connected in Norwegian cultural history.
aulestad_bjornson.popupDesc: Aulestad was the home of Bjørnstjerne Bjørnson and Karoline Bjørnson, and functioned as private home, workplace, farmstead and political-cultural meeting place. Bjørnson was an author, public speaker, social debater and Nobel Prize winner, and the home makes it possible to see how a public figure also lived, wrote, organized and represented himself from a concrete place. In History Go, Aulestad should be used for cultural history, politics, literature, nation-building and the home as a historical stage.

klevfos_cellulose.name: Klevfos Cellulose and Paper Mill
klevfos_cellulose.desc: Former cellulose and paper mill in Løten, in operation from the late 19th century to the 1970s. Klevfos shows wood processing, factory work, hydropower, machinery and workers’ housing in a preserved industrial environment.
klevfos_cellulose.popupDesc: Klevfos is an important industrial museum because it preserves an entire factory world: machines, production lines, hydropower, raw materials, smell, noise, working hours and workers’ housing. Cellulose and paper production linked forest resources to modern industry, and the factory shows how a local community could be built around production. In History Go, Klevfos should be used for labour history, wood processing, industrial technology and the relationship between forest, water and factory.

atlungstad_brenneri.name: Atlungstad Distillery
atlungstad_brenneri.desc: Historic distillery by Lake Mjøsa in Stange, established in the 19th century as part of the history of potatoes, farming and agricultural industry. Atlungstad shows cooperatives, raw materials, production and rural economy.
atlungstad_brenneri.popupDesc: Atlungstad Distillery is a distinctive industrial site in Innlandet because it grew out of agriculture. Potatoes, farmers, cooperative organization, distillation, storage, transport and markets were linked in a production system by Lake Mjøsa. The site should be used in History Go to explain agricultural industry: how farm resources could become industry, how distilleries organized economy and work, and how Lake Mjøsa functioned as a transport and trade space.

norsk_jernbanemuseum_hamar.name: Norwegian Railway Museum Hamar
norsk_jernbanemuseum_hamar.desc: National museum of Norwegian railway history in Hamar, established in 1896. The museum shows locomotives, stations, signals, work, journeys and the railway’s role in the modernization of Norway.
norsk_jernbanemuseum_hamar.popupDesc: The Norwegian Railway Museum in Hamar is a national main site for transport history. The museum brings together locomotives, carriages, station environments, signalling technology and stories of railway work, travel and state-building. In History Go, the site should be used to show how the railway changed distances, working life, communication, trade, timetables, urban growth and the relationship between centre and periphery.

skibladner_gjovik.name: DS Skibladner / Gjøvik quay
skibladner_gjovik.desc: Historic paddle steamer on Lake Mjøsa, launched in 1856 and still in service as a living technical heritage site. Skibladner shows how Lake Mjøsa connected towns, villages, railway, tourism and trade.
skibladner_gjovik.popupDesc: DS Skibladner is one of Innlandet’s clearest transport symbols. The steamship was built for traffic on Lake Mjøsa and made the lake a practical transport route between Hamar, Gjøvik, Lillehammer and other quays. In History Go, Skibladner should be used to explain the inland region’s waterways: steam technology, post, goods, passengers, tourism, railway connections and Lake Mjøsa as historic infrastructure.

gjovik_gard.name: Gjøvik Manor
gjovik_gard.desc: Historic farm and cultural environment in central Gjøvik, linked to farm history, glassworks, urban development and bourgeois culture. The site gives Gjøvik a concrete historic anchor by Lake Mjøsa.
gjovik_gard.popupDesc: Gjøvik Manor lies in the middle of present-day Gjøvik and makes the city’s older layers visible. The site can be read as farmstead, representative home, park, cultural arena and urban-historical junction. In History Go, Gjøvik Manor should be used to show how a settlement by Lake Mjøsa grew through farm resources, trade, glassworks, communication and bourgeois environments before modern urban structure settled over the landscape.

norsk_skogmuseum_elverum.name: Norwegian Forest Museum
norsk_skogmuseum_elverum.desc: National museum of forestry, hunting, fishing and outfield resources in Elverum. The museum shows how the forest has shaped work, technology, economy, nature use and Norwegian social history.
norsk_skogmuseum_elverum.popupDesc: The Norwegian Forest Museum is a central Innlandet site because the forest is one of the region’s major historical basic resources. The museum presents logging, timber floating, hunting, fishing, machines, tools, nature management, outfield use and the forest’s economic importance. In History Go, the site should be used to show how forest is not only nature, but workplace, export base, livelihood, knowledge system, field of conflict and cultural heritage.

glomdalsmuseet_elverum.name: Glomdal Museum
glomdalsmuseet_elverum.desc: Cultural-history museum in Elverum, established to collect and present culture from Østerdalen and Solør. Glomdal Museum shows building traditions, rural life, crafts, Romani history and diversity in the inland region.
glomdalsmuseet_elverum.popupDesc: Glomdal Museum is one of Innlandet’s major open-air and cultural-history museums. The museum shows farms, houses, dress, crafts, rural life and regional history from Østerdalen, Solør and the Glomma landscape. Especially important is also the presentation of the history of the Romani/Tater people. In History Go, Glomdal Museum should be used to show that inland history is not one homogeneous farming culture, but many social groups, minorities, crafts, movement, work and regional identities.

bjerkebaek_undset.name: Bjerkebæk / Sigrid Undset’s home
bjerkebaek_undset.desc: Sigrid Undset’s home in Lillehammer from 1919, where she lived, wrote and organized her home and garden. Bjerkebæk shows literary history, interest in the Middle Ages, women’s lives, public life and heritage work.
bjerkebaek_undset.popupDesc: Bjerkebæk is the author home of Sigrid Undset. She lived here from 1919, wrote here, built up her home and garden, and worked from here as one of Norway’s most important public literary voices. The site should be used in History Go as cultural history, not only literary biography: home, work, Catholicism, interest in the Middle Ages, Nobel Prize, wartime, female public life and later museum preservation belong together.

hegge_stavkirke.name: Hegge Stave Church
hegge_stavkirke.desc: Stave church in Øystre Slidre in Valdres, dated to the early 1200s. Hegge Stave Church shows stave construction, wood carving, local alterations and Valdres as one of Norway’s richest stave-church regions.
hegge_stavkirke.popupDesc: Stave church in Øystre Slidre in Valdres, dated to the early 1200s. Hegge Stave Church shows stave construction, wood carving, local alterations and Valdres as one of Norway’s richest stave-church regions. In History Go, the site should be used to connect place, material culture, local society and the wider historical processes named in the source text.

reinli_stavkirke.name: Reinli Stave Church
reinli_stavkirke.desc: Stave church in Sør-Aurdal, probably from the late Middle Ages, with an older church site and a clear place in Valdres’ stave-church landscape. Reinli shows continuity, a local church site and the long life of the stave tradition.
reinli_stavkirke.popupDesc: Stave church in Sør-Aurdal, probably from the late Middle Ages, with an older church site and a clear place in Valdres’ stave-church landscape. hundorp_dale_gudbrand.desc: Historic farm and assembly landscape at Hundorp, known from the saga tradition about Dale-Gudbrand and Olav Haraldsson. The site must be used as a source-critical Christianization and power landscape, not as a simple legend.
hundorp_dale_gudbrand.popupDesc: Historic farm and assembly landscape at Hundorp, known from the saga tradition about Dale-Gudbrand and Olav Haraldsson. folldal_gruver.name: Folldal Mines
folldal_gruver.desc: Historic mining and industrial landscape in Folldal, with copper mining from the 1700s and later industrial history. The mines show mountain industry, labour, transport, local community and environmental traces.

norsk_utvandrermuseum_ottestad.popupDesc: Museum at Ottestad presenting Norwegian emigration to America and other migration histories. raufoss_industripark_ammunisjon.desc: Industrial site at Raufoss with roots in state ammunition production from the 1890s. The site shows defence industry, metal technology, working life, company town and transition to a modern industrial cluster.
raufoss_industripark_ammunisjon.popupDesc: Industrial site at Raufoss with roots in state ammunition production from the 1890s. lesja_bygdemuseum.name: Lesja Rural Museum
lesja_bygdemuseum.desc: Rural museum in Lesja showing the building traditions, farm life, summer pasture use, crafts and local communities of the mountain villages in upper Gudbrandsdalen.
lesja_bygdemuseum.popupDesc: Rural museum in Lesja showing the building traditions, farm life, summer pasture use, crafts and local communities of the mountain villages in upper Gudbrandsdalen. kvikne_kobberverk.name: Kvikne Copper Works

kvikne_kobberverk.popupDesc: Historic copper works at Kvikne, with roots in 17th-century mining. tolga_os_museum.desc: Local-history museum environment in the Tolga area, with buildings, farmyards and objects from Nord-Østerdalen. The site shows farm life, crafts, mountain-village culture and regional identity.
