In History Go, the site should be used to connect place, material culture, local society and the wider historical processes named in the source text.

hedalen_stavkirke.name: Hedalen Stave Church
hedalen_stavkirke.desc: Stave church in Hedalen in Sør-Aurdal, with a medieval core and rich furnishings. The church shows Valdres stave-church history, forest settlements, local church art, pilgrim traditions and a living church site.
hedalen_stavkirke.popupDesc: Hedalen Stave Church is one of Valdres’ important stave churches and carries traces of both the Middle Ages and later use. Its forest and valley setting makes it a local gathering place, not only architecture. Furnishings, traditions, rebuilding and long use show how a stave church could remain a living place through many historical phases.

vaga_kyrkje.name: Vågå Church
vaga_kyrkje.desc: Church in Vågå with roots in medieval church building and later seventeenth-century rebuilding. Vågå Church shows how older stave-church materials, rural identity and a post-Reformation church interior can meet in one building.
vaga_kyrkje.popupDesc: Vågå Church shows that medieval heritage does not always survive as an unchanged stave church. The present church was rebuilt in the seventeenth century, but has traditions and material traces from older church building. It explains rebuilding, reuse of materials, the Reformation period, rural craft and a local church site with both medieval and early modern layers.

garmo_stavkirke_maihaugen.name: Garmo Stave Church / Maihaugen
garmo_stavkirke_maihaugen.desc: Stave church from Garmo in Lom, moved and rebuilt at Maihaugen. It shows medieval heritage, demolition, collecting, relocation and the open-air museum’s role in Norwegian cultural heritage protection.
garmo_stavkirke_maihaugen.popupDesc: Garmo Stave Church now stands at Maihaugen and makes museum preservation concrete. Originally from Garmo in Lom, it was dismantled, collected and rebuilt in the open-air museum’s landscape. The site explains moved cultural monuments: what is preserved, what changes, how the museum setting shapes experience, and why heritage protection often saved buildings by moving them.

sygard_grytting_pilegrimsgard.name: Sygard Grytting / pilgrim farm
sygard_grytting_pilegrimsgard.desc: Historic farm in Sør-Fron, known as a lodging place along the pilgrim route through Gudbrandsdalen. It shows farming, hospitality, travel, kinship, buildings and pilgrim tradition.
sygard_grytting_pilegrimsgard.popupDesc: Sygard Grytting helps explain the pilgrim route as more than a line on a map. Farms along the way offered shelter, food, control, social contact and practical support to travellers. The site shows how medieval and later travel depended on concrete farms and people, and connects Gudbrandsdalen, pilgrimage, farming, hospitality and historic buildings.

matrand_slagsted_1814.name: Matrand / 1814 battlefield
matrand_slagsted_1814.desc: War-history landscape at Matrand in Eidskog, linked to fighting against Swedish forces in 1814. The site shows border defence, local terrain, mobilization and Norwegian-Swedish conflict history.
matrand_slagsted_1814.popupDesc: Matrand is an important Innlandet site for the history of 1814. While many connect 1814 with Eidsvoll and Moss, Matrand shows that the war was also fought in specific border communities. Terrain, roads, forest, farms and local defence lines mattered, making 1814 both a constitutional year and a year of war.

magnor_glassverk.name: Magnor Glassworks
magnor_glassverk.desc: Historic glassworks at Magnor in Eidskog, by the Swedish border. It shows craft, industry, design, border trade, working life and material culture in an inland borderland.
magnor_glassverk.popupDesc: Magnor Glassworks is an important industrial and craft site in Innlandet. Its position near Sweden makes it relevant as both production environment and border economy. Glassblowing, form-making, design, labour, trade and material knowledge meet in one company history, showing Innlandet’s art-industry and design history.

finnetunet_skogfinsk_museum.name: Finnetunet / Forest Finn museum
finnetunet_skogfinsk_museum.desc: Museum environment in Finnskogen presenting Forest Finn settlement, smoke cabins, slash-and-burn farming, migration, language, cultural encounters and minority history in the Norway-Sweden borderland.
finnetunet_skogfinsk_museum.popupDesc: Finnetunet gives Innlandet a necessary minority and migration perspective. The Forest Finns came from Finnish areas via Sweden and settled in border forests, where slash-and-burn farming, smoke cabins, Finnish language, kin networks, Christianity, local conflict and adaptation shaped distinct cultural environments.

sor_fron_kirke_gudbrandsdalsdomen.name: Sør-Fron Church / Gudbrandsdalsdomen
sor_fron_kirke_gudbrandsdalsdomen.desc: Large octagonal church in Sør-Fron, often called Gudbrandsdalsdomen. It shows church building, local grandeur, craftsmanship, a rural centre and post-Reformation church life in Gudbrandsdalen.
sor_fron_kirke_gudbrandsdalsdomen.popupDesc: Sør-Fron Church is one of Gudbrandsdalen’s most striking church buildings. The large octagonal church from the late eighteenth century shows post-Reformation architecture, local resources, rural power, craftsmanship and congregational needs in a new era, alongside the valley’s better-known medieval layers.

lesja_kirke.name: Lesja Church
lesja_kirke.desc: Eighteenth-century church in Lesja, known for richly carved wooden interiors and local church art. It shows mountain settlements, craftsmanship, church space, rural economy and religious culture in upper Gudbrandsdalen.
lesja_kirke.popupDesc: Lesja Church is a strong mountain-community point in Innlandet’s church history. Its richly carved furnishings and interior show local craft knowledge, religious symbolism and the resources of the rural community. Together with Lesja Bygdemuseum it connects church, farm, mountains, craft, materials and local community in upper Gudbrandsdalen.

valdres_folkemuseum_fagernes.name: Valdres Folk Museum
valdres_folkemuseum_fagernes.desc: Regional folk museum at Fagernes presenting Valdres building traditions, bunad dress, folk music, farm life, crafts, summer-farm culture and social history.
valdres_folkemuseum_fagernes.popupDesc: Valdres Folk Museum is a key place for understanding Valdres as a historical region. Buildings, farmyards, textiles, costumes, crafts, folk music, summer-farm culture, tools and objects make the valley’s everyday life and identity concrete, and link the region’s stave churches, villages, mountain resources and material culture.

odalstunet_sor_odal.name: Odalstunet
odalstunet_sor_odal.desc: Open-air local-history museum environment in Odalen, with buildings, objects and farmyards showing farm life, crafts, work, forest, agriculture and rural community.
odalstunet_sor_odal.popupDesc: Odalstunet gives Odalen a concrete cultural-historical anchor. Farmyard settings, older buildings, tools, interiors and local-history collections show how work, agriculture, forest, crafts, household and local community were organized, and present Odalen as its own historical region between the Glomma, forest settlements and agricultural landscapes.

tynset_bygdemuseum.name: Tynset Bygdemuseum
tynset_bygdemuseum.desc: Local-history museum environment in Tynset showing building traditions, farm life, crafts, household work, summer farming and regional identity in Nord-Østerdalen.
tynset_bygdemuseum.popupDesc: Tynset Bygdemuseum gives Nord-Østerdalen an important local focus beside mining, mountains and travel routes. Buildings, tools and farmyard settings show how farms, households, crafts, summer farming and seasonal work shaped life in the region, presenting Tynset as a local community and cultural region.

eidskog_museum_almenninga.name: Eidskog Museum / Almenninga
eidskog_museum_almenninga.desc: Local-history museum environment in Eidskog, in the same border-history landscape as Matrand and Magnor. It shows farm life, border contact, forest, trade, war history and rural community.
eidskog_museum_almenninga.popupDesc: Eidskog Museum / Almenninga gives a broader local-history frame for Eidskog’s border history. The area links 1814 memories, forest, agriculture, border trade, farm environments and everyday community life, showing that border villages were not only battlefields and customs points, but whole societies living with Sweden as neighbour, resource and political border.

hamar_stasjon_jernbanebyen.name: Hamar Station / railway town
hamar_stasjon_jernbanebyen.desc: Railway environment in Hamar, linked to the city’s modern growth by Lake Mjøsa and to the connection between railway, steamships, trade, station and regional centre.
hamar_stasjon_jernbanebyen.popupDesc: Hamar Station and its railway environment show Hamar as a modern Mjøsa town. After medieval Hamar at Domkirkeodden, nineteenth-century urban growth was shaped by railway, station, trade, steamships, town planning and regional administration. The site links the medieval town with the new railway town.

ringsaker_kirke.name: Ringsaker Church
ringsaker_kirke.desc: Large medieval stone church at Ringsaker, in a rich agricultural and Mjøsa landscape. It shows church power, stone architecture, farm landscapes, pilgrim routes and travel lines on Hedmarken.
ringsaker_kirke.popupDesc: Ringsaker Church is one of Hedmarken’s most important medieval church sites. The monumental stone church stands in a landscape where agriculture, Lake Mjøsa, farm power, travel and religious organization have been linked for centuries, showing wealth, administration, rural centres and regional continuity.

proysenstua_rudshogda.name: Prøysenstua / Rudshøgda
proysenstua_rudshogda.desc: Alf Prøysen’s childhood environment at Rudshøgda, linked to crofter life, work, songs, children’s literature, language and social experience on Hedmarken.
proysenstua_rudshogda.popupDesc: Prøysenstua gives Innlandet an important social and cultural-history site. Alf Prøysen’s texts grew from an environment of crofter holdings, working people, dialect, everyday life, children, humour, hardship and observation, showing how literature and popular culture can be historical sources for class, language, work, childhood and modernization from below.

dovre_kirke.name: Dovre Church
dovre_kirke.desc: Church in Dovre by the travel and pilgrim landscape toward Dovrefjell. The site shows mountain settlements, church site, routes, material use and religious continuity in upper Gudbrandsdalen.
dovre_kirke.popupDesc: Dovre Church is a good historical anchor for the mountain crossing between Gudbrandsdalen and Trøndelag. It lies in a landscape shaped by travel, pilgrim tradition, posting stations, mountain farms, climate and journeys over Dovrefjell, where religion, road, weather, travel and rural community belonged together.

sel_kirke_otta.name: Sel Church / Otta landscape
sel_kirke_otta.desc: Historic church site in Sel, by the Otta and Gudbrandsdalen landscape. It shows a rural centre, travel, church life, farm landscapes and local continuity in mid-Gudbrandsdalen.
sel_kirke_otta.popupDesc: Sel Church gives mid-Gudbrandsdalen a concrete church site. The area around Otta and Sel has been shaped by movement through the valley, agriculture, side roads toward the mountains, rural community and religious organization. Local church sites tied together farms, roads, burial grounds and public functions in the valley settlements.

femundshytten_smeltverk.name: Femundshytten / smelting history
femundshytten_smeltverk.desc: Historic smelting and mining environment by Femunden, linked to copper mining, forest, charcoal burning, transport and mountain resources in the border area toward the Røros region.
femundshytten_smeltverk.popupDesc: Femundshytten shows how mining history could shape remote mountain and forest landscapes. Smelting copper ore required large amounts of forest for charcoal, transport over water and winter roads, workers, supplies and technical knowledge, connecting the Røros-area mining economy, Femunden as transport space, forest resources and small industrial communities.

rendalen_bygdemuseum.name: Rendalen Bygdemuseum
rendalen_bygdemuseum.desc: Local-history museum environment in Rendalen showing farming, forestry, hunting, crafts, building traditions and everyday life in an Østerdalen forest and valley community.
rendalen_bygdemuseum.popupDesc: Rendalen Bygdemuseum gives Rendalen a concrete local-history anchor. The region’s history is closely linked to forest, hunting, fishing, agriculture, summer farming, crafts, rivers and farm environments. The museum shows that Østerdalen consists of many local variants, each with its own farmyards, work forms, material traces and stories.

moelv_stasjon_mjoslinjen.name: Moelv Station / the Mjøsa Line
moelv_stasjon_mjoslinjen.desc: Railway station in Moelv, linked to transport in the Mjøsa villages, timber, farming, commuting, trade and small-town growth between Hamar, Gjøvik and Lillehammer.
moelv_stasjon_mjoslinjen.popupDesc: Moelv Station shows how the railway shaped smaller towns around Lake Mjøsa. Moelv lies in a landscape where the lake, farming, forest resources, sawmills, timber, trade and commuting have been closely connected. In History Go, the site should show that transport history is also about the smaller hubs between the larger towns: stations that changed everyday journeys, goods, work and local identity.

stange_stasjon_dovrebanen.name: Stange Station / Dovre Line
stange_stasjon_dovrebanen.desc: Railway station in Stange, linked to Hedmarken’s agricultural landscape, Lake Mjøsa, freight, post, commuting, local trade and small-town growth.
stange_stasjon_dovrebanen.popupDesc: Stange Station adds a modern transport layer to Stange alongside the medieval church and agricultural industry. The railway made it easier to move people, milk, grain, goods and post between Hedmarken’s farm landscape and larger markets. In History Go, Stange Station should show how the railway changed farming communities: new routines, new centres, faster transport and closer links to the town.

gran_stasjon_gjovikbanen.name: Gran Station / Gjøvik Line
gran_stasjon_gjovikbanen.desc: Railway station at Gran, linked to the Gjøvik Line, Hadeland’s farming, trade, commuting, post, town growth and the connection between Hadeland and the Oslo/Gjøvik markets.
gran_stasjon_gjovikbanen.popupDesc: Gran Station shows Hadeland’s modern transport history. Where Granavollen and the Sister Churches show the Middle Ages and church power, the station shows another historical layer: railway, trade, goods, work journeys, schooling, post and town growth. In History Go, Gran Station should connect old church sites with modern infrastructure and show how Hadeland became more closely integrated into larger regional networks.

lena_stasjon_totenbanen.name: Lena Station / Toten Line
lena_stasjon_totenbanen.desc: Historic station at Lena, linked to the Toten Line, farming, dairy and milk transport, trade, town growth and Østre Toten’s connection to larger markets.
lena_stasjon_totenbanen.popupDesc: Lena Station and the Toten Line make Toten’s transport history concrete. Toten is an agricultural landscape, but farming became modern through logistics: stations, milk, goods, post, work journeys and trade. In History Go, Lena should show how a railway station could link farms, dairies, shops, town centre, school, work and regional markets.

reinsvoll_stasjon_totenbanen.name: Reinsvoll Station / Toten Line
reinsvoll_stasjon_totenbanen.desc: Railway station at Reinsvoll, linked to the Toten Line, connections toward the Skreia/Raufoss area, industry, commuting, freight and town growth in Vestre Toten.
reinsvoll_stasjon_totenbanen.popupDesc: Reinsvoll Station gives Vestre Toten an important transport point. The Toten Line and local branch connections made the area more accessible for industry, farming, commuting and freight. In History Go, Reinsvoll should connect Raufoss’ industrial history with the railway’s practical infrastructure: workers, raw materials, finished products, post, trade and local town growth.

dokka_stasjon_valdresbanen.name: Dokka Station / Valdres Line
dokka_stasjon_valdresbanen.desc: Historic railway point at Dokka, linked to the Valdres Line, trade in the Land region, forestry, farming, post, freight and town growth.
dokka_stasjon_valdresbanen.popupDesc: Dokka Station shows how the Valdres Line served not only Valdres, but also the Land region. The station tied together forestry, farming, trade, post, work journeys and town development at Dokka. In History Go, the site should show how a railway can create regional in-between places: places that are not the terminus, but still gain new importance through the line.

skarnes_stasjon_kongsvingerbanen.name: Skarnes Station / Kongsvinger Line
skarnes_stasjon_kongsvingerbanen.desc: Railway station at Skarnes, linked to the Kongsvinger Line, Odalen, trade in the Glomma region, forestry, commuting, post and town growth.
skarnes_stasjon_kongsvingerbanen.popupDesc: Skarnes Station gives Odalen a transport-history hub. The Kongsvinger Line made Skarnes a place where farms, forest, river, trade, work and journeys were connected to Oslo, Kongsvinger and the border to the east. In History Go, Skarnes should show that the railway created new local centres also in areas otherwise told through farm museums, churches and forestry.

braskereidfoss_kraftverk.name: Braskereidfoss Power Station
braskereidfoss_kraftverk.desc: Power station on the Glomma at Braskereidfoss, linked to modern hydropower, regulation, energy supply, industrial communities, flood risk and technical infrastructure in the Solør/Glomma landscape.
braskereidfoss_kraftverk.popupDesc: Braskereidfoss Power Station gives Solør and the Glomma a modern energy-history point. The Glomma is not only a travel and timber-floating river, but also a regulated power resource with technical facilities, energy production, flood issues and local infrastructure. In History Go, Braskereidfoss should show how modern hydropower changed the river landscape: power, control, risk, local community and environmental history in one place.

slidredomen_vestre_slidre.name: Slidre Cathedral / Vestre Slidre Church
slidredomen_vestre_slidre.desc: Medieval stone church in Vestre Slidre, often called Slidredomen. The church shows Valdres’ medieval history, stone architecture, church power, farm landscape and regional continuity alongside the stave-church landscape.
slidredomen_vestre_slidre.popupDesc: Slidredomen is one of Valdres’ most important medieval church sites. The large stone church shows that Valdres history is not only made up of stave churches, but also of monumental stone churches, regional church centres and local landscapes of power. In History Go, Slidredomen should connect Valdres’ farms, travel routes, church power, stone architecture and religious continuity, and compare the stone churches with the stave churches in the same region.

bruflat_kirke_etnedal.name: Bruflat Church
bruflat_kirke_etnedal.desc: Historic church site in Bruflat in Etnedal, linked to Valdres’ smaller villages, cemetery, local community, farm landscape, travel and church continuity.
bruflat_kirke_etnedal.popupDesc: Bruflat Church gives Etnedal a clear church site in History Go. Etnedal can easily sit in the shadow of larger Valdres sites, but church, cemetery, local museum, farms, roads and meeting places show a distinct rural history. In History Go, Bruflat should cover Valdres’ smaller communities: history exists not only in stave churches and large museums, but in local institutions that organised life, death, community and identity.

skreia_stasjon_totenbanen.name: Skreia Station / Toten Line
skreia_stasjon_totenbanen.desc: Historic station environment at Skreia, linked to the Toten Line, agricultural logistics, trade, town growth, freight, milk transport and the connection between Toten and the Gjøvik/Oslo markets.
skreia_stasjon_totenbanen.popupDesc: Skreia Station shows how a local railway could organise an agricultural landscape. The Toten Line gave Skreia and the surrounding villages new transport options for milk, grain, goods, post and people. In History Go, Skreia should show the importance of the terminus: the line ended there, but the network continued through farms, dairies, shops, roads and markets.

flisa_stasjon_solorbanen.name: Flisa Station / Solør Line
flisa_stasjon_solorbanen.desc: Historic station at Flisa, linked to the Solør Line, forestry, farming, freight, post, trade, town growth and Solør’s role as a Glomma and border region.
flisa_stasjon_solorbanen.popupDesc: Flisa Station makes Solør’s modern transport history concrete. Solør is shaped by forest, farming, the Glomma and border contact, and the railway tied this resource landscape to larger markets. In History Go, Flisa Station should be used together with Solør Museum and Åsnes Church to show how local identity is formed by both older rural life and modern logistics.

vinger_kirke_kongsvinger.name: Vinger Church
vinger_kirke_kongsvinger.desc: Historic church site in Kongsvinger/Vinger, linked to the border town’s church life, fortress town, cemetery, official milieu, local community and the transition from rural district to urban setting.
vinger_kirke_kongsvinger.popupDesc: Vinger Church gives Kongsvinger a church and local-community layer alongside the fortress and the station. The border town was not only military and strategic, but also a place where people lived, died, married, worked and organised community around church and cemetery. In History Go, Vinger Church should show how border history is also social history, official culture and local urban life.

grue_finnskog_kirke.name: Grue Finnskog Church
grue_finnskog_kirke.desc: Church site in Grue Finnskog, linked to Forest Finn settlement, border villages, local community, cemetery, language and cultural encounters, and institution-building in Finnskogen.
grue_finnskog_kirke.popupDesc: Grue Finnskog Church gives Finnskogen a local institutional site alongside the museum history. Forest Finn settlement was not only about smoke cabins and slash-and-burn farming, but also about church, cemetery, school, language, families, local community and relations with the Norwegian/Swedish state and church organisation. In History Go, the site should show minority history as a lived local community over time.

furnes_kirke_ringsaker.name: Furnes Church
furnes_kirke_ringsaker.desc: Historic church site in Furnes in Ringsaker, in Hedmarken’s farming and Mjøsa landscape. The site shows church, cemetery, farm life, local community and continuity between Hamar and Ringsaker.
furnes_kirke_ringsaker.popupDesc: Furnes Church gives Hedmarken a local church site between the larger urban and medieval points. Furnes lies in a landscape where farms, Lake Mjøsa, the Hamar region, Ringsaker and church institutions are closely connected. In History Go, Furnes should show how smaller church sites linked rural communities, families, cemeteries and local meeting places in a rich agricultural area.

alvdal_kirke.name: Alvdal Church
alvdal_kirke.desc: Historic church site in Alvdal, linked to Nord-Østerdalen’s rural communities, farm life, mountain resources, cemetery, local community and church continuity.
alvdal_kirke.popupDesc: Alvdal Church gives Alvdal an institutional historical layer alongside Husantunet. The church stands as a local meeting place in a landscape shaped by farms, mountains, travel, summer farming and Nord-Østerdalen’s regional identity. In History Go, Alvdal Church should show how smaller church sites organised community, rituals, family memory and local institutions in mountain villages.

bjorgan_prestegard_kvikne.name: Bjørgan Parsonage, Kvikne
bjorgan_prestegard_kvikne.desc: Historic parsonage environment at Kvikne, known as Bjørnstjerne Bjørnson’s birthplace. The site connects parsonage, official culture, mountain village, Nord-Østerdalen and Norwegian cultural history.
bjorgan_prestegard_kvikne.popupDesc: Bjørgan Parsonage at Kvikne gives Nord-Østerdalen a clear cultural-history point. The parsonage was a home, official residence, farm environment and social institution, and is especially known as Bjørnstjerne Bjørnson’s birthplace. In History Go, the site should show how parsonages could be cultural and administrative hubs in mountain villages.

kvikne_kirke.name: Kvikne Church
kvikne_kirke.desc: Historic church site at Kvikne, linked to copper mining, mountain village, parsonage, travel and local community in Nord-Østerdalen.
kvikne_kirke.popupDesc: Kvikne Church gives Kvikne an institutional and social historical layer alongside the copper works and Bjørgan Parsonage. The church stood in an environment where mining, farms, mountain resources, clerical authority, cemetery and local organisation were closely interwoven.

oyer_kirke.name: Øyer Church
oyer_kirke.desc: Historic church site in Øyer, linked to Gudbrandsdalen’s rural life, travel, farm landscape, cemetery and church continuity.
oyer_kirke.popupDesc: Øyer Church gives Øyer a local historical anchor alongside the Norwegian Road Museum and the Hunderfossen area. The church site shows how valley communities had their own meeting places, cemeteries, farm networks and public rituals that tied the local community together.

tretten_kirke.name: Tretten Church
tretten_kirke.desc: Historic church site at Tretten in Øyer, linked to the valley’s farms, travel, cemetery, local community and church continuity in Gudbrandsdalen.
tretten_kirke.popupDesc: Tretten Church gives the northern part of Øyer municipality its own historical point. Tretten lies in Gudbrandsdalen’s travel landscape, and the church site shows how smaller rural centres had their own institutions, cemeteries and communities.

skjaak_bygdamuseum.name: Skjåk Rural Museum
skjaak_bygdamuseum.desc: Rural museum in Skjåk presenting farm life, building traditions, mountain resources, irrigation, crafts and local community in a dry and distinctive inland landscape.
skjaak_bygdamuseum.popupDesc: Skjåk Rural Museum gives upper Gudbrandsdalen an important local-history point. Skjåk stands out through its dry climate, irrigation channels, farming adaptation, mountain resources, crafts and distinctive building traditions. In History Go, the museum should show how natural conditions shape history: water, climate, mountains, soil, farms and working knowledge are not background, but the structure of the local community.

stenberg_toten_museum.name: Stenberg / Toten Museum
stenberg_toten_museum.desc: Historic farm and museum environment in Toten, linked to official culture, agriculture, gardens, interiors and local social history.
stenberg_toten_museum.popupDesc: Stenberg / Toten Museum gives Toten a broad social-history point alongside Raufoss and the medieval churches. The farm complex shows official culture, agriculture, gardens, household life, interiors, social rank and local community life. In History Go, the place should show that Toten is not only industry and farming, but also official milieus, representation, education and local power structures.

jorstadmoen_leir.name: Jørstadmoen Camp
jorstadmoen_leir.desc: Military camp near Lillehammer, especially linked to the history of signals and military communications. Jørstadmoen shows defence training, technology, camp life, mobilisation and military modernisation in Innlandet.
jorstadmoen_leir.popupDesc: Jørstadmoen Camp gives Innlandet an important military-history point alongside fortresses and war memorials. The camp is especially linked to signals, communication, training and military organisation. In History Go, Jørstadmoen should explain modern defence as infrastructure and expertise: radio, telephone, command, exercises, camp structure, conscription, specialisation and the relationship between military institution and local community.

nordberg_fort.name: Nordberg Fort
nordberg_fort.desc: Mountain fort in Skjåk, built as part of early twentieth-century defence planning in a mountain and valley landscape. Nordberg Fort shows military control, mountain passes, mobilisation and strategic reading of terrain.
nordberg_fort.popupDesc: Nordberg Fort makes defence history visible in a mountain and valley landscape. The fort shows how military planning concerned roads, mountain passes, valleys, sightlines and control of movement. In History Go, the site should explain defence as terrain reading: why some points gain strategic importance, how installations are built into landscapes, and how local mountain communities formed part of national security plans.

gausdal_bygdetun.name: Gausdal Rural Museum
gausdal_bygdetun.desc: Local-history rural museum in Gausdal with buildings, farmyards, tools and settings that show farm life, crafts, households and rural culture in Gudbrandsdalen.
gausdal_bygdetun.popupDesc: Gausdal Rural Museum gives Gausdal a concrete local-history anchor alongside Aulestad. The buildings and objects show how farms, work, crafts, households, kinship and local community were organised in a Gudbrandsdal village. In History Go, the place should show that cultural history around Gausdal is not only Bjørnson and nation-building, but also everyday life, material culture and local forms of work.

trysil_bygdetun.name: Trysil Rural Museum
trysil_bygdetun.desc: Rural museum in Trysil showing the forest community’s farm life, crafts, timber, hunting, border contact, building traditions and everyday life before modern tourism.
trysil_bygdetun.popupDesc: Trysil Rural Museum is important because Trysil is often associated with skiing and tourism, while the rural museum shows the older forest community. Here History Go can present farms, forestry, hunting, timber, crafts, border contact, winter life and local material traces. The site should be used to make Trysil historical before the tourist economy: a forest and border community with its own work practices and landscape knowledge.

solor_museum_flisa.name: Solør Museum / Flisa
solor_museum_flisa.desc: Local-history museum point in Solør, emphasising forestry, agriculture, farm life, crafts, the Glomma landscape and local identity in south-eastern Innlandet.
solor_museum_flisa.popupDesc: Solør Museum / Flisa gives the Solør region a necessary local-history anchor. Solør lies between the Glomma, forest, agriculture, Swedish border contact and rural communities where forest work, log driving, farm life, crafts and local organisation have been central historical traces. In History Go, the place should show Solør as its own region, not just a transit area between Kongsvinger, Elverum and Finnskogen.

grue_kirke_brannminne.name: Grue Church / fire memorial
grue_kirke_brannminne.desc: Church site in Grue linked to the great church fire of 1822. The place shows local disaster memory, church history, safety, grief, grave markers and community remembrance work.
grue_kirke_brannminne.popupDesc: Grue Church and the memory of the 1822 church fire form a powerful local and national disaster site. The fire struck a gathered congregation and became a dramatic memory of building, safety, crowds, panic, grief and local loss. In History Go, the site should be used carefully as memory history: not sensation, but church, preparedness, rituals, collective grief, grave markers and how local communities process disasters over time.

lom_bygdamuseum_presthaugen.name: Lom Rural Museum / Presthaugen
lom_bygdamuseum_presthaugen.desc: Rural museum in Lom presenting farm life, building traditions, irrigation, mountain resources, crafts and everyday life in Ottadalen and upper Gudbrandsdalen.
lom_bygdamuseum_presthaugen.popupDesc: Lom Rural Museum / Presthaugen complements Lom Stave Church with everyday and rural history. Where the stave church shows a church site and medieval heritage, the rural museum shows farms, houses, work, tools, irrigation culture, use of materials and the practical knowledge of the mountain community. In History Go, the place should explain how the Lom landscape was lived in: through water, soil, summer farms, timber, stone, travel routes and local crafts.

blokkodden_villmarksmuseum.name: Blokkodden Wilderness Museum
blokkodden_villmarksmuseum.desc: Museum environment by Femunden presenting outfield use, hunting, fishing, forest, travel, summer farming and wilderness life in Engerdal and Femundsmarka.
blokkodden_villmarksmuseum.popupDesc: Blokkodden Wilderness Museum gives Engerdal a concrete historical point for outfield and wilderness culture. The area around Femunden has been shaped by fishing, hunting, forestry, summer farming, travel, border contact, Sámi presence and resource use near mining landscapes. In History Go, Blokkodden should show that wilderness is not empty nature, but a historical working landscape with labour, knowledge, traces and conflicts.

husantunet_alvdal_bygdemuseum.name: Husantunet / Alvdal Rural Museum
husantunet_alvdal_bygdemuseum.desc: Historic farm and rural museum in Alvdal showing North Østerdalen’s building traditions, farm life, crafts, summer farming and everyday culture.
husantunet_alvdal_bygdemuseum.popupDesc: Husantunet / Alvdal Rural Museum gives Alvdal a local-history anchor in History Go. Farmyards, buildings and objects show how farm life, work, animal husbandry, crafts, summer farming and households were organised in North Østerdalen. The place should show that regional history is not only major mines and famous writers, but also material culture, local work practices and the everyday structure of rural society.

koppangtunet_stor_elvdal.name: Koppangtunet / Stor-Elvdal Museum
koppangtunet_stor_elvdal.desc: Local-history museum point at Koppang showing farm life, forestry, the Glomma, travel, crafts and everyday culture in Stor-Elvdal.
koppangtunet_stor_elvdal.popupDesc: Koppangtunet / Stor-Elvdal Museum gives central Østerdalen a concrete historical point. Koppang and Stor-Elvdal are shaped by the Glomma, forest, timber, agriculture, travel, station communities and local crafts. In History Go, the place should show how Østerdalen is not one broad forest category, but a series of local valley communities with their own farmyards, work traditions, resource use and institutions.

tylldalen_bygdetun.name: Tylldalen Rural Museum
tylldalen_bygdetun.desc: Rural museum and local-history environment in Tylldalen, with buildings and objects showing farm life, crafts, travel, church-site tradition and North Østerdalen rural culture.
tylldalen_bygdetun.popupDesc: Tylldalen Rural Museum gives a smaller but important local entry point to North Østerdalen history. The valley has old church-site traditions, farm environments, travel routes, crafts and rural culture that make it relevant alongside Tynset and Kvikne. In History Go, the place should show how small valleys can have their own historical centres of gravity, and how local-history farm museums make everyday life, work and travel visible.

faaberg_kirke.name: Fåberg Church
faaberg_kirke.desc: Historic church site in Fåberg, important for the rural history around Lillehammer before and during the town’s growth. The place shows church, farm landscape, graveyard and local continuity.
faaberg_kirke.popupDesc: Fåberg Church gives the Lillehammer area a rural-history anchor outside the town and museum narrative. Before Lillehammer became a town, Fåberg was a local church site and rural community where farms, graveyard, travel and church life bound the community together. In History Go, Fåberg Church should show the relationship between urban growth and older rural districts: Lillehammer did not appear from nowhere, but grew in a landscape with older institutions.

vang_kirke_hamar.name: Vang Church, Hamar
vang_kirke_hamar.desc: Historic church site in Vang by Hamar, linked to Hedmarken’s agricultural landscape, rural community and church continuity around Lake Mjøsa.
vang_kirke_hamar.popupDesc: Vang Church by Hamar provides an important rural-history counterpoint to Domkirkeodden and the modern railway town. The area shows Hedmarken’s farm landscape, local church site, graveyard, families, agriculture and church organisation. In History Go, Vang Church should show that the Hamar region is not only medieval town and modern town, but also older rural districts with their own local continuity.

mesna_kraft_og_industri.name: Mesna power and industrial landscape
mesna_kraft_og_industri.desc: Historic power and industrial landscape along the Mesna river in Lillehammer, linked to hydropower, mills, industry, urban growth and technical modernisation.
mesna_kraft_og_industri.popupDesc: The Mesna river and Lillehammer’s power and industrial traces show how natural power became urban history. The river supported mills, small industry, electricity, hydropower and urban development. In History Go, Mesna should connect Lillehammer’s cultural and museum profile with technical and economic history: behind the town also lie water, drops, turbines, factories, labour and municipal modernisation.

lillehammer_bryggeri_historisk_miljo.name: Lillehammer Brewery / historic industrial environment
lillehammer_bryggeri_historisk_miljo.desc: Historic brewery and urban industrial environment in Lillehammer, linked to local production, labour, trade, raw materials, water and the town’s growth as a regional centre.
lillehammer_bryggeri_historisk_miljo.popupDesc: Lillehammer Brewery as a historic industrial environment offers another entry to the town than Maihaugen, Bjerkebæk and Olympic or tourism history. Brewing is about raw materials, water, production, labour, distribution, serving culture, urban economy and local identity. In History Go, the site should show everyday urban industry: small and medium-sized production environments that built workplaces and city life around practical goods.

kistefos_tresliperi_jevnaker.name: Kistefos Wood Pulp Mill / industrial museum
kistefos_tresliperi_jevnaker.desc: Historic wood pulp mill by the Randselva at Jevnaker, later an industrial museum and cultural environment. Kistefos shows wood processing, hydropower, working life, technology, ownership and reuse of industrial landscapes.
kistefos_tresliperi_jevnaker.popupDesc: Kistefos is a strong industrial-history point in Innlandet. The pulp mill used hydropower from the Randselva and linked forest resources, machines, paper raw material, workers, capital and transport into a modern production environment. In History Go, Kistefos should be used as industrial history first: the art and museum profile is important, but the place must also be read as hydropower-driven wood processing, workplace and technical heritage.

kapp_melkefabrikk.name: Kapp Milk Factory
kapp_melkefabrikk.desc: Historic milk factory by Lake Mjøsa at Kapp, linked to dairy industry, agriculture, transport, processing and Toten’s modernisation as an agricultural region.
kapp_melkefabrikk.popupDesc: Kapp Milk Factory gives Toten an important agro-industrial site. Milk, farms, deliveries, processing, packaging, workers, technology and Lake Mjøsa as a transport landscape were linked in one production system. In History Go, Kapp should show that agricultural history is not only fields and farms, but also factories, cooperatives, industrial processing, working life and markets.

loiten_braenderi.name: Løiten Distillery
loiten_braenderi.desc: Historic distillery at Løten, linked to potato cultivation, agricultural industry, distillation, working life, cooperative economy and local production environments on Hedmarken.
loiten_braenderi.popupDesc: Løiten Distillery is a clear example of how agriculture became industry. Potatoes, farms, raw-material deliveries, distillation, storage, workers, transport and brand-building belong together in one historical production environment. In History Go, the site should be used soberly as agricultural and industrial history, not as alcohol nostalgia: the point is raw-material economy, technology, labour and local value creation.

land_museum_dokka.name: Land Museum Dokka
land_museum_dokka.desc: Local history museum environment at Dokka presenting farm life, forestry, crafts, buildings, everyday life and regional identity in the Land region.
land_museum_dokka.popupDesc: Land Museum gives Nordre Land and the Land region a historical anchor in History Go. The museum presents buildings, objects, crafts, farming, forestry, households and local communities in an area between Valdres, Hadeland, Toten and Gjøvik. The site should be used to show local transitions: forest and agriculture, inland transport, rural communities and regional identity.

vang_stavkirke_tomta_valdres.name: Vang stave church / original church site
vang_stavkirke_tomta_valdres.desc: Original church site of Vang stave church in Valdres, before the church was sold, moved and rebuilt in present-day Poland. The site shows cultural heritage protection, loss, relocation, national romanticism and Valdres stave-church history.
vang_stavkirke_tomta_valdres.popupDesc: Vang stave church is one of the most dramatic examples of relocated medieval heritage. The church originally stood in Vang in Valdres, but in the nineteenth century it was dismantled, sold and later rebuilt in Karpacz in present-day Poland. In History Go, the original church site should be used to ask what a cultural monument is when the building is moved: place, materials, use, identity, loss, preservation and international memory history.

nord_odal_bygdetun_sand.name: Nord-Odal rural museum / Sand
nord_odal_bygdetun_sand.desc: Local history rural museum in Nord-Odal showing farm life, forest, agriculture, crafts, buildings and everyday culture in Odalen.
nord_odal_bygdetun_sand.popupDesc: Nord-Odal rural museum at Sand gives the northern part of Odalen its own historical coverage. The farmyard, buildings and objects can be used to show forestry, agriculture, crafts, households, school, local community and the relationship to Storsjøen and the transport lines in the area. In History Go, the site should be used as a local counterpart to Odalstunet in Sør-Odal, so that Odalen is not treated as one undifferentiated region.

valer_kirke_brannminne.name: Våler church / fire memorial
valer_kirke_brannminne.desc: Church site in Våler, known for older church history and more recent fire and reconstruction history. The site shows church, local community, loss, architecture, memory work and new use of a historic place.
valer_kirke_brannminne.popupDesc: Våler church as a historic site should be used carefully and precisely. The church site has older local significance, and the more recent fire made the place a strong local memory of loss, grief, reconstruction and debate about architecture and use. In History Go, Våler should be used to show how church sites can change form while still retaining meaning: cemetery, memories, rituals, rural community and new architecture lie on top of older historical layers.

tingelstad_gamle_kirke.name: Tingelstad old church
tingelstad_gamle_kirke.desc: Medieval stone church at Tingelstad in Gran, in Hadeland’s old agricultural and church-site landscape. The church shows local stone architecture, farm landscape, ecclesiastical continuity and Hadeland’s medieval depth.
tingelstad_gamle_kirke.popupDesc: Tingelstad old church gives Hadeland another concrete medieval point alongside Granavollen and Lunner. The old stone church stands in a landscape where farms, church, travel, land and local power have been connected for centuries. In History Go, Tingelstad should show that medieval history is found not only in the best-known monuments, but also in smaller church sites carrying local continuity and regional patterns.

fluberg_kirke.name: Fluberg church
fluberg_kirke.desc: Historic church site by Randsfjorden in Søndre Land. Fluberg church shows church life, farm landscape, fjord travel, cemetery and local continuity in the Land region.
fluberg_kirke.popupDesc: Fluberg church gives Søndre Land a concrete church site in History Go. Its location by Randsfjorden makes the place historically interesting as part of a landscape where fjord, farms, travel, agriculture and local community met. In History Go, Fluberg should cover the Land region’s everyday and church-site history: not only museums and larger settlements, but also local institutions that bound the rural communities together.

biri_kirke.name: Biri church
biri_kirke.desc: Historic church site in Biri by Mjøsa, connected to rural history, farm life, travel, cemetery and local continuity in northern Gjøvik municipality.
biri_kirke.popupDesc: Biri church is a local but important historical point in the Mjøsa landscape. Biri lies between Gjøvik, Lillehammer and Ringsaker, and the church site shows how rural communities along Mjøsa had their own institutions, cemeteries, family memories and transport links. In History Go, Biri should cover the historical space between the larger town and museum sites around Mjøsa.

mustad_hunnselva_gjovik.name: Mustad / Hunnselva industrial environment
mustad_hunnselva_gjovik.desc: Historic industrial environment along the Hunnselva in Gjøvik, connected to the Mustad company, metal goods, fishhooks, labor, hydropower, exports and the city’s industrial development.
mustad_hunnselva_gjovik.popupDesc: The Mustad and Hunnselva environment is one of Gjøvik’s most important traces of industrial history. The river supplied power, the town supplied labor, and the company developed from local production into international industry. In History Go, the site should show how a town by Mjøsa also became an industrial town: hydropower, metalworking, factory labor, export goods, owner families, worker communities and technical expertise belong together.

brumunddal_molle_industri.name: Brumunddal mill / industrial environment
brumunddal_molle_industri.desc: Historic mill and industrial environment in Brumunddal, connected to agriculture, grain, hydropower, local processing, labor and settlement growth in Ringsaker.
brumunddal_molle_industri.popupDesc: Brumunddal mill / industrial environment gives Ringsaker a point for labor and settlement history. Mills and small industry turned the agricultural landscape into production, trade and workplaces. In History Go, the site should show how Brumunddal developed through grain, processing, river, workshops, station, workers and local markets, not only as a modern settlement by the E6 and Mjøsa.

bagn_bygdesamling.name: Bagn local heritage collection
bagn_bygdesamling.desc: Local history collection in Bagn presenting Sør-Aurdal’s farm life, crafts, everyday culture, war history, forest, agriculture and Valdres identity.
bagn_bygdesamling.popupDesc: Bagn local heritage collection gives Sør-Aurdal a broader historical anchor alongside Hedalen stave church and Bagnsbergatn. Collections, buildings and objects show everyday life, farming, crafts, local economy, forest, agriculture and memory work in Valdres. In History Go, Bagn should connect war history and stave-church history with ordinary lives and local material traces.

etnedal_bygdetun_bruflat.name: Etnedal rural museum / Bruflat
etnedal_bygdetun_bruflat.desc: Rural museum in Etnedal showing farm life, mountain-rural community, crafts, summer farming, forest, agriculture and local identity in a smaller Valdres municipality.
etnedal_bygdetun_bruflat.popupDesc: Etnedal rural museum gives Etnedal its own place in the Innlandet data. The region can easily disappear between larger Valdres sites, but the rural museum shows farms, forms of work, summer farming, forest, crafts, households and local stories. In History Go, the site should show that small municipalities and valleys also have their own historical structures, not only as part of a broad Valdres category.

brandval_kirke.name: Brandval church
brandval_kirke.desc: Historic church site in Brandval north of Kongsvinger, in a forested landscape close to the Glomma. The site shows local church history, farms, cemetery, forestry and rural community.
brandval_kirke.popupDesc: Brandval church gives the Kongsvinger region a local church site outside fortress and town history. Brandval lies in a landscape shaped by the Glomma, forest, farms, travel and proximity to the border. In History Go, the site should show how churches bound together forest villages and farm communities, and how the Kongsvinger area consists of more than fortress, border war and urban environment.

hjerkinn_fjellstue.name: Hjerkinn mountain lodge
hjerkinn_fjellstue.desc: Historic mountain lodge and travel site at Dovrefjell, connected to the pilgrim route, king’s road, posting services, lodging and the mountain crossing between Eastern Norway and Trøndelag.
hjerkinn_fjellstue.popupDesc: Hjerkinn mountain lodge is an important point in the history of travel across Dovrefjell. Mountain lodges were necessary infrastructure in a demanding landscape: they provided lodging, food, posting services, rest and safer passage for pilgrims, officials, traders and other travelers. In History Go, Hjerkinn should show that mountains were not only natural barriers, but historical transport spaces with institutions, routes, work and risk.

budsjord_pilegrimsgard.name: Budsjord pilgrim farm
budsjord_pilegrimsgard.desc: Historic farm environment in Dovre, used as a pilgrim farm along Gudbrandsdalsleden. Budsjord shows farm, lodging, travel, building preservation and local continuity in the Dovre community.
budsjord_pilegrimsgard.popupDesc: Budsjord pilgrim farm shows how the pilgrim route depended on concrete farms, farmyards and people. The farm lies in the Dovre community, where travel toward Dovrefjell required food, lodging, route knowledge and social organization. In History Go, Budsjord should connect farm history with travel history: pilgrimage was not only walking, but also being part of a network of houses, roads, landscapes and local hospitality.

jutulheimen_vagaa_bygdamuseum.name: Jutulheimen / Vågå rural museum
jutulheimen_vagaa_bygdamuseum.desc: Rural museum in Vågå presenting farm life, building traditions, crafts, irrigation, mountain resources and everyday culture in Ottadalen.
jutulheimen_vagaa_bygdamuseum.popupDesc: Jutulheimen / Vågå rural museum complements Vågå church with local everyday and rural history. Buildings, tools and the farmyard environment show how people lived with mountain, valley, soil, water, summer farming, crafts and travel. In History Go, the site should show Vågå as more than a church site: a local community where practical knowledge, use of materials and adaptation to landscape formed the basis of history.

follebu_kirke.name: Follebu church
follebu_kirke.desc: Medieval stone church in Follebu in Gausdal, connected to farm landscape, village center, ecclesiastical continuity and Gudbrandsdalen’s local medieval history.
follebu_kirke.popupDesc: Follebu church gives Gausdal a medieval church site alongside Aulestad and the rural museum. The old stone church shows how Gausdal was part of Gudbrandsdalen’s ecclesiastical and social landscape long before the great nation-building narratives of the nineteenth century. In History Go, Follebu should connect the Middle Ages, farm landscape, stone architecture, village center and local continuity.

heidal_kirke.name: Heidal church
heidal_kirke.desc: Church and historic church site in Heidal, connected to the valley’s building traditions, local community, fire and reconstruction history, and Gudbrandsdalen’s ecclesiastical continuity.
heidal_kirke.popupDesc: Heidal church should be used as a historic church site and reconstruction case. Heidal has strong local building traditions and valley identity, and the church site shows how a local community can carry church tradition onward even when buildings burn, are rebuilt or raised anew. In History Go, the site should ask about continuity: what remains of a church site when the building has changed form, and how does new architecture express local tradition?

hoff_kirke_toten.name: Hoff church Østre Toten
hoff_kirke_toten.desc: Large medieval stone church in Østre Toten, in a rich agricultural landscape by Mjøsa. Hoff church shows church power, farm structure, stone architecture and Toten’s historical weight.
hoff_kirke_toten.popupDesc: Hoff church is one of Toten’s most important medieval sites. The large stone church stands in an agricultural landscape where farms, church, families, land and local power are connected. In History Go, Hoff should strengthen Toten’s historical profile: Toten is not only industry and agricultural modernization, but also an old church-site landscape with medieval stone churches and strong local continuity.

gjovik_glassverk_historisk_miljo.name: Gjøvik glassworks / historic environment
gjovik_glassverk_historisk_miljo.desc: Historic glassworks trace in Gjøvik, connected to the city’s early economic base, farm environment, Mjøsa trade, crafts, production and urban development.
gjovik_glassverk_historisk_miljo.popupDesc: Gjøvik glassworks is a key to understanding Gjøvik’s early urban history. Before Gjøvik became a modern Mjøsa town with station, industry and urban institutions, there were production environments that used resources, crafts, trade and the location by Mjøsa. In History Go, the site should be used as a historical layer together with Gjøvik farm, Skibladner and Mustad/Hunnselva: the town grew through several overlapping economic tracks.

eina_stasjon_totenbanen.name: Eina station / Toten Line
eina_stasjon_totenbanen.desc: Railway station and transport point on the Toten Line, connected to agriculture, industry, commuting, freight, settlement growth and the link between Toten and the Gjøvik/Oslo system.
eina_stasjon_totenbanen.popupDesc: Eina station and the Toten Line show how the railway changed Toten. Stations created new hubs for goods, milk, people, mail, work and local markets. In History Go, Eina should show that transport history is not only main lines and national museums, but also small stations that changed everyday life, agriculture, industry and settlement structure.

aurdal_kirke.name: Aurdal church
aurdal_kirke.desc: Historic church site in Aurdal in Valdres, with an 18th-century church, burial ground, farm landscape and local continuity. The site shows church life and a village centre in Valdres beyond the stave-church icons.
aurdal_kirke.popupDesc: Aurdal church gives Nord-Aurdal a historic church site alongside Valdres Folkemuseum and Fagernes. The church shows how post-Reformation church buildings, burial ground, village centre, farms, roads and local community shaped everyday religious and social history. In History Go, Aurdal should be used to show that Valdres history is not only stave churches, but also later church sites that carried local communities through new layers of time.

nes_kirke_ringsaker.name: Nes church Ringsaker
nes_kirke_ringsaker.desc: Medieval church site at Nes in Ringsaker, in Mjøsa’s agricultural and travel landscape. The site shows stone architecture, farm power, church continuity and local institutions in Hedmarken.
nes_kirke_ringsaker.popupDesc: Nes church in Ringsaker gives the Mjøsa landscape another historic church point among Hedmarken’s major sites. The church and church site show how farming districts by Mjøsa had their own religious, social and local institutions. In History Go, Nes should be used to show that medieval Hedmarken consisted of several church sites and power landscapes, not only Hamar, Stange and Ringsaker church.

lillehammer_kirke.name: Lillehammer church
lillehammer_kirke.desc: Town church in Lillehammer from the 19th century, connected to urban growth, market-town status, public space, the bourgeoisie and the institutions of the modern town.
lillehammer_kirke.popupDesc: Lillehammer church gives the town history a central institutional point. As Lillehammer grew as a market town and regional centre, it needed a church, public spaces, meeting places and symbolic buildings. In History Go, the church should be used to show the town’s 19th-century layer: Lillehammer is not only Maihaugen, Bjerkebæk and an Olympic town, but also a modern small town with church, school, trade, industry, station and municipal development.

ullinsvin_vagaa_prestegard.name: Ullinsvin / Vågå parsonage
ullinsvin_vagaa_prestegard.desc: Historic parsonage environment in Vågå, closely connected to the church site, official culture, land, local institutions, garden, building environment and Gudbrandsdalen’s social history.
ullinsvin_vagaa_prestegard.popupDesc: Ullinsvin / Vågå parsonage gives Vågå a layer of official and institutional history beside the church and the village museum. Parsonages were not only residences, but farming, administration, education, church power, hospitality, garden culture and building culture. In History Go, Ullinsvin should be used to show how the parsonage tied church, state, local community and landscape together in a valley district.

bjorge_gard_ringebu.name: Bjørge farm Ringebu
bjorge_gard_ringebu.desc: Historic farm environment in Ringebu, connected to Gudbrandsdalen’s farm landscape, buildings, agriculture, family lineages, local work and social continuity.
bjorge_gard_ringebu.popupDesc: Bjørge farm in Ringebu gives Gudbrandsdalen a farm-history point beside the stave church, pilgrimage and larger museum sites. Farms are basic cells in the valley’s history: land, kinship, houses, farmyards, work, livestock, forest, mountain pasture and local status belong together. In History Go, the site should be used to show how valley history is not only about travel and churches, but also about concrete farm environments that carried economy and social order.

espedalen_nikkelverk.name: Espedalen nickel works
espedalen_nikkelverk.desc: Historic nickel works in Espedalen, connected to 19th-century mining, mountain resources, smelting history, labour, transport and industrial community in Gausdal.
espedalen_nikkelverk.popupDesc: Espedalen nickel works shows that Gudbrandsdalen and the surrounding mountain areas were not only agriculture, travel routes and churches, but also industrial and mining landscapes. The nickel works’ history connects ore, smelting, forest, charcoal, transport, capital, workers and local effects. In History Go, the site should be used to explain how mountain resources could create industrial points far from coast and city, and how such enterprises changed local communities and landscapes.

fagernes_stasjon_valdresbanen.name: Fagernes station / Valdres Line
fagernes_stasjon_valdresbanen.desc: Historic railway point at Fagernes, terminus of the Valdres Line and important for freight, tourism, post, trade and Valdres’ connection to the rest of Eastern Norway.
fagernes_stasjon_valdresbanen.popupDesc: Fagernes station and the Valdres Line show how the railway changed Valdres. The line made it easier to move people, goods, post, agricultural products and tourists between the valley and larger markets. In History Go, the site should be used to show transport as regional transformation: a station could change the centre, tourism, trade, sense of time and the relationship between mountain district and city market.

lillehammer_stasjon.name: Lillehammer station
lillehammer_stasjon.desc: Railway station in Lillehammer, connected to urban growth, the forerunners of the Dovre Line, Mjøsa and valley traffic, tourism, trade and regional transport.
lillehammer_stasjon.popupDesc: Lillehammer station is an important point in urban and transport history. The railway strengthened Lillehammer’s role as a regional centre and made the town more accessible for trade, work, journeys, tourism and later major events. In History Go, the station should be used to connect the museum town, industrial town and tourist town: the infrastructure made the town a hub between Mjøsa, Gudbrandsdalen and the rest of Eastern Norway.

rena_leir.name: Rena camp
rena_leir.desc: Modern military camp by Rena, connected to Army training, exercises, professionalisation, camp structure and defence restructuring in Innlandet.
rena_leir.popupDesc: Rena camp gives Innlandet a modern point of defence history. Where fortresses and older camps show earlier forms of defence, Rena shows how late-20th-century and newer military organisation required large training areas, specialised education, infrastructure, logistics and a close connection between military institution and local community. In History Go, Rena should be used to ask about modern defence as organisation, not as battlefield.

sanderud_sykehus_historisk_omrade.name: Sanderud hospital / historic area
sanderud_sykehus_historisk_omrade.desc: Historic hospital area in Stange, connected to the institutional history of psychiatry, health work, buildings, workplaces and changing treatment ideals in the 20th century.
sanderud_sykehus_historisk_omrade.popupDesc: Sanderud hospital must be treated as health and institutional history, not as a sensational site. Large hospital areas shaped patient lives, treatment ideals, workplaces, architecture, local communities and public health policy. In History Go, Sanderud should be used carefully to ask how society has understood mental health, care, control, institutions, rights and the scaling down and restructuring of large treatment environments.

romedal_kirke.name: Romedal church
romedal_kirke.desc: Historic church site in Romedal in Stange, with an older church-site tradition and later church buildings. The site shows Hedmarken’s rural landscape, church life, rebuilding, burial ground and local continuity.
romedal_kirke.popupDesc: Romedal church should be used as church-site history more than as a single date. The site has older ecclesiastical continuity in a rich agricultural landscape, while the present church represents later rebuilding and local institution-building. In History Go, Romedal should show how church sites can preserve meaning even when buildings change form: burial ground, farms, families, roads and local community provide continuity.

snertingdal_kirke.name: Snertingdal church
snertingdal_kirke.desc: Historic church site in Snertingdal, northwest in Gjøvik municipality. The site shows a forest district, farm life, church life, burial ground, local identity and smaller villages’ place in the history of the Mjøsa region.
snertingdal_kirke.popupDesc: Snertingdal church gives the Gjøvik region a forest-district perspective. Not all history around Mjøsa is about town, glassworks, steamships and industry; smaller villages such as Snertingdal had their own church sites, farms, forest resources, family memories and local communities. In History Go, Snertingdal should be used to expand the Gjøvik data from town and Mjøsa shore to forest district and local continuity.

dombas_stasjon_jernbaneknutepunkt.name: Dombås station / railway junction
dombas_stasjon_jernbaneknutepunkt.desc: Railway junction at Dombås, where the Dovre Line and Rauma Line make the mountain village a central transport point between Eastern Norway, Trøndelag and Romsdal.
dombas_stasjon_jernbaneknutepunkt.popupDesc: Dombås station shows how the railway could make a mountain place into a national junction. The Dovre Line and Rauma Line linked valleys, mountain crossings, freight, post, travel, military mobility and tourism. In History Go, Dombås should be used to explain transport as landscape transformation: station, hotel, settlement, trade and traces of war history belong together in one railway environment.

biri_glassverk_historisk_sted.name: Biri glassworks / historic site
biri_glassverk_historisk_sted.desc: Historic glassworks trace in Biri, connected to 18th-century glass production, crafts, forest resources, transport and industrial history in the Mjøsa region.
biri_glassverk_historisk_sted.popupDesc: Biri glassworks is a good example of older inland industry. Glass production required energy, raw materials, specialists, transport and a market, and the Mjøsa region provided both resources and connections. In History Go, Biri glassworks should connect crafts, forest, furnaces, labour, Mjøsa and regional industrial history, and compare older glassworks traces with Hadeland, Magnor and Gjøvik glassworks.

otta_stasjon_gudbrandsdalen.name: Otta station / Gudbrandsdalen
otta_stasjon_gudbrandsdalen.desc: Railway station at Otta, central to settlement growth, trade, post, freight, travel and connections between Gudbrandsdalen, Ottadalen and the mountain areas.
otta_stasjon_gudbrandsdalen.popupDesc: Otta station shows how the railway created and strengthened settlements in Gudbrandsdalen. The station connected the valley, side roads toward Vågå, Lom and Skjåk, goods, tourism, post, work journeys and local markets. In History Go, Otta should show transport as a settlement engine: the station changed the centre, trade and the relationship between mountain villages and larger networks.

kongsvinger_stasjon_grensebanen.name: Kongsvinger station / border line
kongsvinger_stasjon_grensebanen.desc: Railway station in Kongsvinger, connected to the Kongsvinger Line, border connections, urban growth, trade, military strategy and the link toward Sweden.
kongsvinger_stasjon_grensebanen.popupDesc: Kongsvinger station gives the fortress town a modern transport layer. Kongsvinger was already strategically important through the fortress and the border, but the railway changed the town’s economy, travel routes, flow of goods and connections toward Sweden. In History Go, the station should be used to show how border history is not only war and fortress, but also trade, labour, railway, post, commuting and international connection.

kvam_krigsminne_1940.name: Kvam / war memorial 1940
kvam_krigsminne_1940.desc: War-history site in Kvam in Gudbrandsdalen, connected to the fighting in April 1940. The site shows the valley’s military importance, civilian experiences, destruction, memorial work and local war history.
kvam_krigsminne_1940.popupDesc: Kvam in Gudbrandsdalen is an important place for understanding the war in 1940 as valley and local-community history. The fighting in Gudbrandsdalen involved terrain, roads, delay, civilians, destruction and small places that suddenly gained military importance. In History Go, Kvam should be used soberly to show how the Second World War was experienced in villages and valleys, not only in the capital, fortresses and national decision-making rooms.

asnes_kirke.name: Åsnes church
asnes_kirke.desc: Historic church site in Åsnes in Solør, connected to forest, agriculture, the Glomma region, burial ground, local community and church continuity in southeastern Innlandet.
asnes_kirke.popupDesc: Åsnes church gives Solør a local church site in History Go. The area is shaped by forest, agriculture, the Glomma, small settlements, farms and border and travel lines. The church should be used to show how local institutions tied the Solør villages together: baptism, burial, gathering, kinship, school, public rituals and rural identity. It complements Solør museum with a concrete ecclesiastical and social centre of gravity.

hof_kirke_asnes.name: Hof church Åsnes
hof_kirke_asnes.desc: Historic church site in Hof in Åsnes, connected to Solør’s rural communities, burial ground, farm life, forest, agriculture and local community.
hof_kirke_asnes.popupDesc: Hof church in Åsnes should be used as part of Solør’s local church-site history. Solør consists of several villages and church sites, not only one regional museum point. Hof shows how church, farms, burial ground, forest, agriculture and local meeting places structured everyday life. In History Go, the site should be used to give Solør denser local coverage, with precise placement in Åsnes and a clear distinction from other Hof sites in Norway.

tolga_kirke.name: Tolga church
tolga_kirke.desc: Historic church site in Tolga, connected to Nord-Østerdalen’s rural communities, mining-adjacent regional history, burial ground, local organisation and church continuity.
tolga_kirke.popupDesc: Tolga church gives Tolga an institutional point beside the village museum and regional museum history. The church stands in a landscape shaped by farms, mountains, a mining-adjacent economy, travel routes and small local communities with strong meeting places. In History Go, Tolga church should be used to show how church sites functioned as social and administrative centres in Nord-Østerdalen, not only as religious buildings.

brugata_storgata_rusmiljo.name: Brugata / Storgata – the open drug scene
brugata_storgata_rusmiljo.desc: The Brugata/Storgata intersection is a bounded social territory in Oslo's open drug scene, with Storgata 33 as a stable map anchor. Official, research and community sources describe it as a marketplace, a social meeting place and a contact surface with services, control and urban development.
brugata_storgata_rusmiljo.popupDesc:
This place is the bounded social territory in and near the Brugata/Storgata intersection, anchored at Storgata 33. It is not the whole of Storgata or Brugata, the Folketeater quarter, the historical Plata site or Prindsen reception centre. Oslo's municipal Byplan article describes both a major open market for illegal drugs and a social meeting place; that dual role is the canonical core.

The scene has moved over time. The Association for Humane Drug Policy links the present situation to systematic dispersal from 2011, when people and activities were pushed away from Oslo Central Station and later moved among Brugata/Storgata, Elgsletta and the Hausmann area. This is a present territory in a history of displacement, not a new name for Plata.

The 2020 KORUS report “Unsafe marketplace” used fieldwork and interviews. It documents insecurity, violence and a market, but also social contact and belonging. No visible person may therefore be identified as part of the scene, dependent on drugs, a seller, a buyer or a service user.

The arcade at Storgata 33 is a physical focus in the municipal analysis. The Storgata renewal completed in 2021 changed tracks, pavements and technical infrastructure, but physical design alone did not resolve perceived insecurity. A social territory emerges through space, relationships, market, services, control and displacement together.

A Bykuben mapping project published in 2025 reached nearly 35 people through several meeting places. Friendship and nature along the Akerselva river were highlighted as resources. This is why knowledge must come through respectful participation and aggregated accounts, not close observation of people in the street.

In 2025 the Association for Humane Drug Policy argued for a sheltered outdoor place to stay, explicitly distinct from a lawless zone. The revised budget provided no funding and legal clarification was still under way.

On site, read only architecture, street profile and public connections from ordinary paths. Do not photograph, follow, approach or map people, times, transactions, health information or routes. The place is documented; visible people are never collectibles or evidence.

paulus_kirke.name: Paulus Church
paulus_kirke.desc: Paulus Church is an active brick church by Birkelunden, consecrated in 1892 and designed by Henrik Bull with forms inspired by German Gothic architecture. It belongs to Grünerløkka's planned urban structure and parish life and was protected in 2006. The church and park remain separate places.
paulus_kirke.popupDesc: Paulus Church stands at Thorvald Meyers gate 31 opposite Birkelunden. Henrik Bull designed the red-brick church, consecrated in 1892, with a high narrow entrance tower, pointed arches, a longitudinal plan and short transepts. The church was protected with the Birkelunden environment in 2006. It remains an active place of worship and also hosts concerts and cultural activities, so its history must be read together with its current use.

freia_fabrikken.name: Freia Chocolate Factory
freia_fabrikken.desc: The Freia factory at Rodeløkka is an industrial site where chocolate production, work organization, branding and employee welfare have been combined since 1889. Freiaparken and Freiasalen made art and recreation physical parts of the workplace.
freia_fabrikken.popupDesc: Freia was founded at Rodeløkka in 1889 and was acquired by Johan Throne Holst in 1892. The brick factory expanded together with production, distribution and advertising. Ole Sverre designed Freiaparken in 1922 and Freiasalen, completed in 1934 with twelve paintings by Edvard Munch. The hall and park were protected in 2015, while the site remains connected to chocolate production in Oslo.
